claims.claim: Q4 revenue was $90.0 billion.
Revenue increased 18% year-over-year.
Revenue increased 17% in constant currency.
Operating income was $40.6 billion.
Operating income increased 18% year-over-year.
Net income was $35.8 billion on a GAAP basis.
GAAP net income increased 31% year-over-year.
Net income was $35.3 billion on a non-GAAP basis.
Non-GAAP net income increased 22% year-over-year.
Diluted earnings per share was $4.81 on a GAAP basis.
GAAP diluted earnings per share increased 32% year-over-year.
Diluted earnings per share was $4.74 on a non-GAAP basis.
Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share increased 23% year-over-year.
Microsoft Cloud revenue was $59.3 billion.
Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 27% year-over-year.
Productivity and Business Processes revenue was $37.8 billion.
Productivity and Business Processes revenue increased 14% year-over-year.
Intelligent Cloud revenue was $39.3 billion.
Intelligent Cloud revenue increased 32% year-over-year.
Intelligent Cloud revenue increased 31% in constant currency.
More Personal Computing revenue was $12.9 billion.
More Personal Computing revenue decreased 4% year-over-year.
More Personal Computing revenue decreased 5% in constant currency.
Microsoft will provide forward-looking guidance during the earnings conference call.
The company returned $10.2 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases in Q4.
Total assets increased to $758.4 billion as of June 30, 2026, from $619.0 billion as of June 30, 2025.
The guidance to be provided during the conference call is guidance for the next fiscal year.
claims.note: The release says only that Microsoft will provide 'forward-looking guidance' and 'certain forward-looking information' on the call; it does not state that the guidance covers the next fiscal year.

claims.claim: The release outlines potential risks and uncertainties including competition, regulatory changes, and cybersecurity threats.
